old.name: Rue d'Enfer at dusk
old.label: GEM
old.text: Beaune's inner streets have names that say what they are: rue Paradis, rue d'Enfer — Hell Street, the coldest in town, because the wine cellars beneath regulate it. At dusk on a weekday it is deserted; the venting slats breathe cool air even in July. The sound of wine resting underground is the silence you hear. Where the cellar streets When 19:00-20:00 on a weekday

old.hook: The Beaune man who photographed motion and pre-figured cinema
old.text: The Beaune man who photographed motion and pre-figured cinema EUR 6 (combined ticket) WALK-IN Afternoon Installed in the bastioned Porte Marie de Bourgogne, the town's museums honour two Beaune-born figures: Félix Ziem, the painter of Venetian light, and Étienne-Jules Marey, the physiologist whose chronophotography — capturing a body or a bird across a single plate — was a direct ancestor of the moving image. A quiet, surprising stop two minutes from the wine streets. Where Porte Marie de Bourgogne, boulevard Perpreuil

old.name: Hôtel-Dieu — Hospices de Beaune
old.label: MONUMENT
old.hook: A hospital for the poor, paid for by vines, for 528 years
old.text: A hospital for the poor, paid for by vines, for 528 years EUR 12.50 WALK-IN Morning Founded in 1443 by Nicolas Rolin, chancellor of Burgundy, and Guigone de Salins, as a free hospital for the poor — and it stayed one until 1971. The roof of glazed polychrome tiles, laid in chevrons of amber, black and green, is the image of Beaune. Inside, the 72-metre Grande Salle des Pôvres keeps its curtained box-beds and its painted vault. The institution still owns 60 hectares of vines and funds itself, in part, by the November auction. Allow 90 minutes; arrive at opening. Where Centre — Place de la Halle

old.name: Van der Weyden — The Last Judgment
old.label: MASTERPIECE
old.hook: Fifteen Flemish panels, weighed souls, gold scales
old.text: Fifteen Flemish panels, weighed souls, gold scales included with the Hôtel-Dieu WALK-IN Morning Rolin commissioned the Last Judgment polyptych from Rogier van der Weyden, the supreme Flemish painter of the age, for the hospital's chapel. Fifteen painted panels: Christ enthroned on a rainbow, the Archangel Michael weighing souls in golden scales, the blessed and the damned parting left and right. It still hangs in the Hôtel-Dieu, shown with a magnifying mirror so you can read the faces of the saved and the lost. Where inside the Hôtel-Dieu

old.text: A Cluniac nave and five tapestries of the Life of the Virgin free (church) · small fee for the tapestries WALK-IN All day One of the last great Romanesque churches of Burgundy, Cluniac in inspiration, built from the 12th century with Gothic and Renaissance additions. Behind the choir hang the Vie de la Vierge — five Tournai tapestries in wool and silk, completed around 1500, astonishingly preserved. The tapestries show on a restricted schedule (afternoons, April–October); the nave is open and, on a weekday morning, empty. Where Place Général Leclerc
